newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle sales near standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle sales near standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle sales Friday were at a near standstill following moderate sales this week, feedlot sources said.
Packers reportedly were well supplied with cattle after last week's record sales in the Panhandle and large sales in Kansas and were not aggressive this week, they said.
Slipping boxed beef prices this week also kept fed cattle prices from going higher than $72.00 per cwt when they did trade at midweek. The price was unchanged from last week's tops, sources said.
A sale of 100 head was reported in Kansas at $72.00 per cwt Friday -- too light to consider a market test, sources said.
Boxed beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.01 to $0.61, with heavyweight choice cuts down $0.61 at $104.34. The heavyweight choice price fell $1.56 this week.

Showlists next week were expected to have some carryover from this week, but not enough to weigh on the market. Also many cattle on this week's showlists were 'green', or unfinished, and could use a few extra days on feed, market sources said.
